fullPassage: When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!” “Hello,” Aaron answered shyly. “I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?” “Zambezi?” “It’s the name we gave the little elephant.” So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart beating faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, flashed through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat. Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, reached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly warm. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm. “How are you?” Aaron whispered. He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them curiously. “Here,” Samuel whispered, handing a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.” Aaron had seen enough babies nurse to know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, looking Aaron in the eyes as he did. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day he first met the elephant. The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly. Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool. After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked. A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old ... found the mother ... killed ... poachers ....” The men loaded the elephant into the truck. Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.” When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made. The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw. Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours. Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel. But mothers worry, and so did Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian frown, Aaron’s stomach got tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well that medicine couldn’t cure everything. One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to where Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap. After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine. It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable. He had been preparing himself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm. Bezi was getting better each day. His sunken skin slowly gave way to a round belly, and his cheeks filled out, too. Before long, he was moving around more, even trying to leave his stall. The other orphans approached curiously, prodding him all over with their trunks. Eventually, Bezi was allowed to venture outside. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk. Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

det.korean: ② has never left → had never left: 과거 시점 기준의 경험 → 과거완료
det.analysis:
✅ ① injured: '다친' 코끼리라는 수동 의미의 과거분사가 명사 수식 — 적절
❌ ② has never left → had never left: 이야기 전체가 과거 시제이고, '(그때까지) 이렇게 오래 혼자 둔 적이 없었다'는 과거 시점 이전까지의 경험이므로 현재완료가 아닌 과거완료(had + p.p.)가 와야 한다 ← 정답
✅ ③ had happened: What if 뒤에서 '(이미) 일어났다면 어쩌지'라는 과거 사실에 대한 가정 — 과거완료 적절
✅ ④ had been preparing: 달려가기 전부터 계속 마음의 준비를 해 오던 중이었으므로 과거완료진행 — 적절
det.tip: 기준 시점이 과거면 그 이전의 경험·완료는 had + p.p.(과거완료)

det.korean: ③ worse → better: 너는 우리보다 '더 나은' 운이 있기를
det.analysis:
✅ ① curiously: 사무엘이 소년과 코끼리의 교감을 '신기한 듯' 지켜보았다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ rushed: 아론의 기억이 코끼리를 처음 만난 날로 '급히 되돌아갔다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 실패해 온 사육사들이 새로 온 아론에게 기대 → better luck(더 나은 운)

det.korean: ① felt ashamed → felt proud: 베지가 우유를 다 먹으면 '뿌듯함'을 느낌
det.analysis:

✅ ② joked: '나는 코끼리 엄마가 되어 가고 있어'라고 '농담했다'는 문맥에 적절

det.tip: 정성껏 돌본 베지가 우유를 다 먹음 → proud(자랑스러운), ashamed 아님

det.analysis: 사무엘은 '우리보다 운이 좋을지도 모른다(Maybe you will have better luck than we've had)'며 우유병을 건넸고, 잠베지가 아론의 눈을 바라보며 병을 빨기 시작하자 놀라서 고개를 저었다(shook his head in amazement). 사육사들이 못 해낸 일을 아론이 해낸 것이므로 참(T).

det.tip: as free, wild animals(자유로운 야생 동물로서) → roam(돌아다니다)

questions.passage: As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly. Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 창고(pool shed)에서 밧줄과 갈퀴를 가져온 뒤 물에 뛰어들었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 아론이 어미 코끼리를 찾아 둘러보았지만 다른 코끼리는 보이지 않았다(no other elephants in sight)
❌ ② 곧바로 뛰어든 것이 아니라 먼저 정원사의 오두막으로 달려가 도움을 청하고 창고에서 도구를 챙겼다
✅ ③ 창고(pool shed)로 달려가 밧줄과 갈퀴를 챙겼고(grabbed a rope and a rake), 돌아온 뒤 갈퀴를 데크에 내려놓고 물로 곧장 뛰어들었다 ← 정답
❌ ④ 물에 가장 먼저 뛰어든 사람은 정원사가 아니라 아론 자신이다
det.tip: He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake → 그 후 jumped straight into the water

ch: 아론은 어미 코끼리가 지켜보는 가운데 새끼 코끼리를 발견했다.
아론은 이상한 소리를 듣자마자 곧바로 수영장에 뛰어들었다.
아론은 창고에서 밧줄과 갈퀴를 챙겨 돌아온 뒤 물에 뛰어들었다.
정원사가 가장 먼저 수영장 물속으로 뛰어들어 코끼리를 붙잡았다.

questions.passage: Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.” When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made. The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 첫 며칠 밤은 쉽지 않았고 거의 잠들지 못했다
det.analysis:
✅ ① 사육사장은 '일손이 부족하고(We're short on workers) 네가 동물을 잘 다루는 것 같다'며 일자리를 제안했다
✅ ② 어머니는 '아버지도 나처럼 자랑스러워했을 것'이라며 지지했다
✅ ③ 어머니가 '물론 쉬는 날에는 집에 오게 될 것'이라고 말했다
❌ ④ 첫 며칠 밤은 쉽지 않았고(not easy) 아론은 거의 잠을 자지 못했다(hardly slept at all) ← 정답
det.tip: The first few nights ~ were not easy / hardly slept at all

ch: 사육사장은 일손이 부족하다며 아론에게 함께 일할 것을 제안했다.
어머니는 아버지도 자랑스러워했을 것이라며 아론의 취직을 지지했다.
아론은 쉬는 날에는 집에 다녀가기로 했다.
아론은 고아원에서 보낸 첫 며칠 밤 동안 깊고 편안하게 잠들었다.

questions.passage: Aaron ①<u>awoke</u> from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy ②<u>whom rescued</u> Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it ③<u>seems</u> you’re good with animals.” When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision ④<u>was made</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② whom → who: 관계사절 안에서 주어 역할 → 주격 관계대명사
det.analysis:
✅ ① awoke: awake의 과거형 자동사(생각에서 깨어났다) — 적절
❌ ② whom → who: 관계사절 안에서 rescued의 주어 역할을 하므로 목적격 whom이 아니라 주격 관계대명사 who가 와야 한다(you are the boy who rescued Bezi) ← 정답
✅ ③ seems: it seems (that) ~ 구문의 3인칭 단수 현재형 — 적절
✅ ④ was made: his decision이 '내려진' 것이므로 수동태 — 적절
det.tip: 관계사절에서 동사(rescued)의 주어가 비어 있으면 주격 who

questions.passage: On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap. After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine. It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 수의사가 덫에 다친 새 코끼리의 다리에 발라 준 천연 치유 요법을 본문에서 찾아 2단어로 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: green clay (초록 진흙)
det.analysis: 수의사는 덫에 걸려 발에 상처를 입은 새 코끼리의 다리를 초록 진흙(green clay)으로 덮어 주었고, 본문은 이를 a natural healing remedy(천연 치유 요법)라고 설명한다. 따라서 답은 green clay 2단어.
det.tip: covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy

questions.passage: Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, flashed through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat. Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, reached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly warm.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 병들어 야윈 잠베지의 모습을 빗댄, '쭈글쭈글한 뼈 자루'라는 뜻의 표현을 본문에서 찾아 5단어로 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: a wrinkled bag of bones (쭈글쭈글한 뼈 자루)
det.analysis: 짚 위에 누워 담요에 덮인 잠베지의 야윈 모습을 본문은 He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones(그는 쭈글쭈글한 뼈 자루처럼 보였다)라고 비유한다. 조건이 5단어이므로 관사 a를 포함해 a wrinkled bag of bones로 쓴다.
det.tip: looked like + 명사구 비유 표현

questions.passage: One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener __________ (pull) from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: pulling (현재분사)
det.analysis: pull(당기다) → pulling: 'with + 목적어 + 분사'의 부대상황 구문으로, 요리사와 정원사가 가장자리에서 '당기고 있는' 능동 상태이므로 현재분사 pulling이 와야 한다. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge = 요리사와 정원사가 가장자리에서 당기는 가운데.
det.tip: with + 목적어 + 현재분사(능동)/과거분사(수동) — 여기서는 능동이므로 pulling

questions.passage: Eventually, Bezi was allowed to venture outside. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk. Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 고아 코끼리를 돌보는 소년의 헌신과 꿈
det.analysis:
❌ ① 밀렵은 배경 사건일 뿐 이 단락의 중심 내용이 아님
❌ ② 코끼리들의 위계 구조는 언급되지 않음
✅ ③ 아론이 도움이 필요한 아기 코끼리 곁에서 자며 밤낮없이 돌보고, 모든 고아 코끼리가 자유로운 야생 동물로 살아가 고아원이 필요 없어지는 날을 꿈꾼다는 내용 ← 정답
❌ ④ 운영난·인력 부족은 이 단락에 나오지 않음
det.tip: still sleeps near ~ around the clock + dreams of a time when ~

ch: 야생 동물 밀렵이 근절되지 않는 경제적 배경
무리 생활을 하는 코끼리의 사회적 위계 구조
고아 코끼리를 돌보는 소년의 헌신과 그가 꿈꾸는 미래
코끼리 고아원이 겪는 만성적인 운영난과 인력 부족

questions.passage: The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw. Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 낯선 생활에 적응하며 돌봄에 애착을 갖게 됨
det.analysis:
✅ ① 첫 며칠 밤은 잠도 못 자고 집을 그리워했지만, 오래지 않아 베지 곁에서 위안을 찾고 사육사들에게 약 먹이기·채혈 요령을 배우며 적응해 갔다는 내용 ← 정답
❌ ② 힘들어했지만 일을 포기하려 한 적은 없음
❌ ③ 사무엘과 다른 사육사들은 오히려 요령을 가르쳐 주었음(showed him tricks)
❌ ④ 베지는 여전히 매우 아파서 하루 대부분을 잤음(still very sick)
det.tip: not easy → But it wasn't long before ~ find comfort(전환) + showed him tricks(배움)

ch: 아론은 낯선 고아원 생활에 적응하며 베지를 돌보는 일에 애착을 갖게 되었다.
아론은 고된 업무와 향수병 때문에 사육사 일을 포기하려 했다.
사육사들은 텃세를 부리며 아론에게 일을 가르쳐 주지 않았다.
베지는 아론이 오기 전에 이미 건강을 완전히 회복한 상태였다.

questions.passage: What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable. He had been preparing himself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. He __________. Aaron laughed with relief.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 [조건]에 맞게 빈칸을 (영어로) 쓰시오.

그는 몇 개의 플라스틱 병에 닿으려고 애쓰고 있는 것처럼 보였다.

[조건] (1) reach, some, be, trying, plastic, seemed, to, bottles 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 9단어로 쓸 것 (to는 두 번 사용)

det.korean: seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles
det.analysis: 구문 분석: seem + to부정사 구문에서 '~하고 있는 것처럼 보이다'는 진행의 의미를 살려 seem to be -ing로 쓴다. 주어 He + seemed(~처럼 보였다) + to be trying(애쓰고 있는 중) + to reach(닿으려고, try to-V) + some plastic bottles(목적어). try to-V는 '~하려고 애쓰다'는 뜻으로 to reach가 이어진다.
det.tip: seem to be -ing(~하고 있는 것처럼 보이다) + try to-V(~하려고 애쓰다)

questions.wa: seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles
